name: county-changes-1790-1990
title: Historical county changes, 1790–1990
description: Richard L. Forstall's Population of States and Counties of the United States: 1790 to 1990 (U.S. Bureau of the Census, 1996) is an important research resource for anyone who works in economic history. Counties have changed over the course of history. New counties have emerged and some have been abolished. Forstall compiled every major change the Census Bureau recorded: counties formed, abolished, merged, split, or renamed. The trouble is that it is a book, and a tedious one, so researchers who use it usually code up the years they need and stop. I had an LLM read the whole thing and turn it into one machine-readable file, free to use under CC BY 4.0. As a check on accuracy, I compared it with the county changes that Martha Bailey and Andrew Goodman-Bacon coded by hand for their 2015 paper. For every one of their changes that comes from this book, this file reproduces their coding exactly.

sources.title: Forstall, Richard L. (1996). Population of States and Counties of the United States: 1790 to 1990. U.S. Bureau of the Census.

fields.name: event_id
fields.description: The item in the read: p{scan page}-t{table}-r{row}-c{claim} for a Notes-column entry, p{page}-f{footnote}-c{claim} for a footnote.

fields.name: state
fields.description: State name, upper case.

fields.name: unit
fields.description: county, parish, borough, city or subdivision.

fields.name: county
fields.description: The unit's name as the book prints it in its table row, e.g. "Nuckolls (old)".

fields.name: county_fips
fields.description: FIPS code from the book's Part IV. A county abolished before 1930 carries the book's own code, the preceding county's code plus a decimal (38011.1), explained at the foot of every state page; blank where Part IV has no line.

fields.name: event_type
fields.description: birth, abolition, rename, boundary_change, reported_with or other.

fields.name: partner_county
fields.description: The other unit named in the event, as resolved to a table row where possible.

fields.name: partner_unit
fields.description: The partner's unit.

fields.name: partner_state
fields.description: The partner's state (a few partners are across a state line).

fields.name: partner_fips
fields.description: The partner's FIPS code, as for county_fips.

fields.name: partner_role
fields.description: origin, minor_origin (the book's semicolon: a very small contribution), destination, minor_destination, other_name, reporting_unit or counterpart; blank with no partner.

fields.name: census_before
fields.description: The census before the event, in the state's own sequence (Oklahoma has 1907, Alaska 1929 and 1939). Equal to census_after when the event is dated to a census; blank when undated.

fields.name: census_after
fields.description: The census after the event.

fields.name: event_year
fields.description: The year, where the book prints one.

fields.name: when
fields.description: The book's dating phrase as printed: "after 1980", "1840-50", "December 7, 1990".

fields.name: population_moved
fields.description: The population the book attaches to the event, where it gives one.

fields.name: pdf_page
fields.description: The page of the scan.

fields.name: printed_page
fields.description: The book's printed page.

fields.name: location
fields.description: "Notes column", "Note 5", or "Note C31" (a Virginia independent-city note).

fields.name: quote
fields.description: The book's words for this event, verbatim.

fields.name: confident
fields.description: Whether the reader was sure of the item; every doubt was then settled by the author's rulings, so all true.

fields.name: reason_code
fields.description: The kind of doubt the reader had, kept for the record: print, syntax, typing or placement.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: The reader's doubt in words.

fields.name: ruled
fields.description: The author's ruling that settled the doubt, quoting it.

fields.name: corrected
fields.description: Whether a hand correction was applied (none were).

fields.name: checked
fields.description: The date of the ruling.

fields.name: state
fields.description: State name, upper case.

fields.name: unit
fields.description: county, parish, borough, city or subdivision.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The unit's name as the book prints it.

fields.name: present
fields.description: The censuses at which the book gives the unit a population, space-separated.

fields.name: see_notes
fields.description: The note numbers the unit's Notes cell points to.

fields.name: pages
fields.description: The scan pages of the unit's table rows.

fields.name: sections
fields.description: The table section the unit sits under, where the state's table has sections (e.g. Inhabited Islands).

fields.name: n_rows
fields.description: The number of table rows read for the unit (one per census table it appears in).

fields.name: notes
fields.description: The Notes cell, verbatim.

fields.name: first_census
fields.description: The first census in present.

fields.name: last_census
fields.description: The last census in present.

fields.name: gaps
fields.description: Censuses between first and last at which the unit has no population row.

fields.name: unit_key
fields.description: main, or city for Virginia's independent cities under their own Part IV heading.

fields.name: p4_first_census
fields.description: Part IV's first census for the unit.

fields.name: no_change_since
fields.description: Part IV's census since which there has been no significant change.

fields.name: fips
fields.description: Part IV's FIPS code, as for county_fips above (decimal codes for counties abolished before 1930).

fields.name: part4_id
fields.description: The Part IV line the unit was matched to.
